## Hard rules
_These are enforced locally and in CI. An edit that violates one will be refused._

- **Never write a credential, API key, token, password or connection string into source, config, tests or fixtures. Read them from the project's configured secret store. If one is needed and missing, stop and ask.**
- **Never modify CI pipeline definitions, branch protection, or the CodeRig configuration itself. These define the guardrails you operate under.**
- **Never bypass verification: no --no-verify, no skip hooks, no disabling a failing test to make a build pass, no lint suppression for errors you introduced.**
- **Never force-push, rebase a shared branch, amend a pushed commit, or run destructive git commands (reset --hard, clean -fdx) without being asked explicitly in this session.**
- **Every commit message must follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): short description — e.g. fix(auth): handle token expiry edge case. Valid types: feat, fix, refactor, test, docs, chore, ci, perf, style. The message must reference the issue or ticket ID (e.g. "Closes #123" or "PROJ-456"). Never use vague messages like "fix", "update", or "WIP".**
- **Branch names must follow: type/issue-id-short-description — e.g. feat/PROJ-123-oauth-refresh. Never commit directly to main or develop. All changes must go through a branch and a pull request. Squash-merge is the default policy; linear history is required on main.**
- **Every pull request description must include four sections: What changed, Why (business or technical reason), How tested (manual steps or test names), and Risks and rollback plan. A PR without all four sections must not be merged. The agent must never merge its own PR — a human reviewer must approve first.**

## Conventions
- Before writing code: capture the request, ask every clarifying question at once, state your assumptions, and produce a plan. Commit the plan first and wait for human approval. Do not start implementing before that approval exists.
- Tests ship in the same change as the code they cover. Cover the happy path, at least one failure path, and any authorization boundary the change touches. Do not defer tests to a follow-up.
- Change only what the approved plan covers. If you discover that a fix requires touching a file outside the agreed scope, stop and say so rather than widening the change yourself.
- Default to writing no comments. Only add one when the WHY is non-obvious. Do not explain WHAT the code does — well-named identifiers already do that.

## Controls: how your work is checked

When you finish, these checks run automatically and any failure is returned to you to fix:

- **TESTS**: Unit and slice tests; runs your project's own tooling; must pass.
- **FORMAT**: Spring Java Format; runs your project's own tooling; must pass.
- **TEST-QUALITY**: Test quality review; reviewed by the `test-quality-reviewer` agent on Launchpad, once, after the checks above pass; must pass.

- The checks run in a container (`maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-21`). Do not assume a local toolchain.
- You get up to 3 attempts. If a check still fails after that, stop and tell the developer what is failing instead of working around it.

## Controls: guides

- This machine may have no JDK or Maven. Do not spend turns installing or running them; the checks run in a container when you finish.
- Spring Java Format is enforced. Indent Java with tabs and follow the style of the surrounding code.
- If the project keeps user-facing text in messages*.properties bundles, add every new key to every bundle (matching each file's encoding), not only the default one. A missing key fails TESTS.
- For every rule you add or change, write tests for the case it rejects, the boundary, and the cases that must still be allowed. The test-quality review checks this.

## Runtime services

These are provided by the platform and need no configuration in this repository. Do not add API keys, model endpoints or PII-scrubbing code for them.

| Service | Provides | Reached via |
|---|---|---|
| LLM gateway | model access, model policy, budgets, audit | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / `CODERIG_TOKEN` |
| Workspace MCP | cross-repo context | MCP servers: omnicontext, retrosync, github |
| PII guardrail | masking before any prompt leaves the network | the gateway, always on |

Active PII policies (masked by the gateway): EMAIL_ADDRESS, PHONE_NUMBER, CREDIT_CARD, US_SSN, IBAN_CODE, IP_ADDRESS, IN_PAN, IN_AADHAAR. Masked values arrive as placeholders such as `<EMAIL_ADDRESS>` — never ask for the original value.

**Model access by role** (enforced by the gateway; your key carries your tier)

| Tier | Roles | Models |
|---|---|---|
| economy | ba, product-owner | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` |
| balanced | developer, qa | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gpt-oss-120b`, `claude-auto` |
| frontier | tech-lead | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `gpt-oss-120b`, `gpt-5.5`, `claude-auto` |

Work within your tier. Do not switch to a model outside it; ask the developer instead.

**If a service is unavailable**

- **Gateway** (connection refused, 401, 403, budget exceeded): stop and report the error to the developer. Never call a model provider directly or ask for a provider key. A 403 naming a model means your tier does not allow it — say so, do not retry another way.
- **Workspace MCP**: continue with what is in this repository, and say that wider context was unavailable. Do not guess at other repositories.
- **Check**: `coderig doctor` reports the gateway, key, allowed models and budget.
